text:
Marco: Heads-up — EU1 queue depth is growing fast for rw-14b-quant-v2. p50 latency up, admission control started dropping lower-priority requests.
ops-bot: metric snapshot: ```model: rw-14b-quant-v2
region: eu1
queue_depth: 1432
active_slots: 248/320
admission_rejections: 18/min
p50_latency: 420ms
p95_latency: 1.8s
```
Anya: which routes are hitting it? customer-facing or internal batch?
Marco: mostly public API routes and a few low-tier customer aliases. High-volume prompt templates are the hotspot.
Kai: can we switch low-tier traffic to rw-7b-quant-fallback automatically? We have policy for that but not enabled for this model group.
Sophia: fallback sounds right. But note cost delta if we spin more 7b VMs in eu1 vs shift to us-west. Need to check cross-region egress limits.
Marco: quick attempt to rebalance p-slots: ```infractl pslot reassign --region eu1 --model rw-14b-quant-v2 --from-pool general --to-pool burst-temp --slots 24```
Anya: will that preempt any Dedicated customers?
Marco: no, burst-temp is the spare pool, not Dedicated. But it will reduce headroom elsewhere.
ops-bot: recent node events: ```Node/gpu-eu1-19 Warning Eviction ThresholdExceeded pods: 12
Node/gpu-eu1-22 Warning DevicePressure GPU memory 92%
Scheduler info: backpressure policy active for model-group: rw-14b```
Kai: temporary mitigation plan: 1) enable fallback-route to rw-7b for freemium, 2) tighten per-key RPS for non-enterprise, 3) enable prefix KV caching for repeated prompts. I'll push rate-limit delta if folks agree.
Sophia: agree on 1 & 2. On 3, we need to ensure cache warm doesn't spike write-through. Maybe enable for top-10 prompt templates only.
Anya: I'm seeing 60% of rejections are from two customers doing streaming-heavy workloads. Can we reach out and throttle them independently?
Marco: I'll open a DM and flag SEs. Also adding a quick `kubectl` snapshot for context: ```kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep rw-14b | wc -l -> 62 pods
kubectl top pods | grep rw-14b | sort -nr | head -5 -> pod/gw-14b-1 980Mi
```
Kai: I'll apply the rate-limit change for tier=free in 5m: `rlctl update --scope free --model rw-14b-quant-v2 --rps 0.5`
Sophia: I'll prepare a traffic-shift to rw-7b in the routing layer: canary 10% now, 50% in 15m if metrics look good.
ops-bot: scheduled autoscaler action: `increase_min_replicas rw-7b 10 -> 20 (eu1)` queued by autoscaler manager.
prod-alert-bot: INCIDENT created: INC-2026-184555 — EU1 queue depth for rw-14b impacting lower tiers. Link: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-184555
Marco: thanks. Quick postmortem checklist: 1) confirm fallback successful, 2) confirm targeted rate-limits applied, 3) run p-slot rebalance if backpressure persists, 4) follow up with customers. I'll update incident with actions.
Anya: ping me after canary shift, I'll watch rejections and p95.
Kai: applied rate-limit, monitoring now.
Sophia: canary live at 10% — initial latency on rw-7b looks stable.
Marco: nice. If queue_depth doesn't drop within 25m we'll escalate to emergency capacity (spin new nodes).
